```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
```

Powermean estimates conditional power means of nonnegative outcomes. The
mean order `omega` defines the estimand. At order one the target is the
arithmetic mean, and at order zero it is the geometric mean. The working
variance order `tau` defines the estimating equation at nonzero mean orders.

## 1. Fit ordinary power means

The example uses a binary regressor and a continuous control. The
linear index is a log conditional mean. Frequencies of zero outcomes
matter when choosing the estimation sample.

```{r ordinary}
library(powermean)
set.seed(20261120)

n <- 800L
data <- data.frame(treated = rbinom(n, 1, 0.4), control = rnorm(n))
data$outcome <- rpois(n, exp(0.5 + 0.35 * data$treated + 0.2 * data$control))

arithmetic <- ppml(outcome ~ treated + control, data)
geometric <- logols(outcome ~ treated + control, data, positive_only = TRUE)
tidy(arithmetic)
effect(arithmetic, "treated")
```

The exponentiated treated coefficient minus one gives the proportional
change in the arithmetic mean when treatment changes from zero to one,
holding the other regressors fixed. The geometric fit conditions on positive
outcomes here. Its sample record gives the input rows used for estimation.

## 2. Prepare rows and reuse the design

Prepare data once when fitting alternative admitted equations to the
same formula. The fit applies its mean-order domain and records exclusions
on the original input-row scale.

```{r prepared}
prepared <- prepare(outcome ~ treated + control, data)
half_order <- fit(prepared, omega = 0.5, tau = 1.5, vcov = "HC3")
c(n_arithmetic = arithmetic$sample$nobs, n_half_order = half_order$sample$nobs)
head(predict(half_order))
se(half_order)
```

## 3. Estimate a three-way gravity model

The panel has exporter-year, importer-year and directed pair fixed
effects. An agreement takes effect on different dates for different
pairs. Keep the pair classification separate from the two date
interactions.

```{r gravity}
gravity <- expand.grid(exporter = seq_len(12L), importer = seq_len(12L),
                       year = seq_len(8L))
gravity <- gravity[gravity$exporter != gravity$importer, ]
gravity$pair <- interaction(gravity$exporter, gravity$importer, drop = TRUE)
adoption <- sample(2:12, nlevels(gravity$pair), replace = TRUE)
gravity$agreement <- as.integer(gravity$year >= adoption[as.integer(gravity$pair)])
gravity$trade <- rpois(nrow(gravity), exp(1.5 + 0.4 * gravity$agreement +
    sin(gravity$exporter * gravity$year) / 5 + cos(gravity$importer * gravity$year) / 5))

formula <- trade ~ 0 + agreement | pair + exporter^year + importer^year
joint <- ppml(formula, gravity, cluster = ~pair)
cancelled <- fit(formula, gravity, cancel = "pair", tau = 1)
etable(joint, cancelled, names = c("Joint PPML", "Pair-cancelled PPML"))
```

At PPML weighting, pair cancellation gives the profiled joint slope
equation on the common sample. Cancelling at another working variance
changes the equation. Use `fixef()` to inspect normalized retained
effects and recovered group scales. Both models return fitted means
and response residuals on the retained rows.

For a fixed-effect counterfactual, keep the original retained row
labels and supply replacement covariates in fitting order.
`predict()` holds offsets and recovered fixed effects fixed.

```{r gravity-prediction}
retained <- gravity[cancelled$sample$positions, , drop = FALSE]
with_agreement <- transform(retained, agreement = 1L)
head(cbind(fitted = predict(cancelled),
           with_agreement = predict(cancelled, with_agreement),
           residual = residuals(cancelled)))
```

See the Three-Way Gravity with Powermean vignette for sample accounting
and the bias adjustments.

## 4. Difference out two fixed effects with Jochmans GMM

Jochmans GMM estimates an exogenous exponential mean with two
fixed-effect blocks. Use a complete rectangular panel with one row per
cell, two simple identifier columns and at least two levels per block.
Observed zero outcomes remain in the array. A two-by-two panel has
only one rectangle and cannot supply usable covariance.

```{r gmm-rectangular}
panel <- expand.grid(origin = 1:5, destination = 1:6)
cell <- seq_len(nrow(panel))
panel$agreement <- sin(cell)
panel$trade <- exp(0.2 * panel$agreement + panel$origin / 8 -
    panel$destination / 9) * (1 + 0.15 * cos(1.3 * cell))

two_way <- trade ~ 0 + agreement | origin + destination
gmm1 <- fit(two_way, panel, estimator = "gmm1")
gmm2 <- fit(two_way, panel, estimator = "gmm2", start = coef(gmm1))
etable(gmm1, gmm2, uncertainty = "ci")
```

GMM1 and GMM2 use different moment equations. GMM1 can supply a
starting value for GMM2 in the same coefficient order. Both report a
certified local solution with cell-projection covariance and normal
intervals. Conditional on the full regressor array and fixed effects,
the moments require unit means and unit expected products for the
multiplicative errors at opposite cells of each rectangle. The reported
inference assumes conditional independence of observed cells and
growth in both dimensions.

For a directed cross-section, supply every ordered non-self link
among at least four agents and use the same labels in both identifier
columns. Select `fe_layout = "directed"`.

```{r gmm-directed}
dyads <- expand.grid(origin = 1:6, destination = 1:6)
dyads <- dyads[dyads$origin != dyads$destination, ]
cell <- seq_len(nrow(dyads))
dyads$agreement <- sin(cell)
dyads$trade <- exp(0.2 * dyads$agreement + dyads$origin / 8 -
    dyads$destination / 9) * (1 + 0.15 * cos(1.3 * cell))

directed <- fit(two_way, dyads, estimator = "gmm2", fe_layout = "directed")
stata <- with_vcov(directed, "stata")
cbind(paper = se(directed), stata = se(stata))
head(cbind(fitted = predict(directed), residual = residuals(directed)))
```

The paper covariance is the default. The Stata view applies
`(n - 1) / n` to the directed covariance for `n` agents and leaves the
slopes at the fitted point. Prediction recovers the two sets of fixed
effects with the GMM slopes held fixed. Use `fixef()` to inspect them.

## 5. Retain inference for another covariance request

Use a covariance view to change the requested inference while keeping
the estimated point. Save the result if the same retained rows and
influences are needed in a later R session.

```{r retained}
alternative <- with_vcov(arithmetic, "HC3")
cbind(default = se(arithmetic), HC3 = se(alternative))
```
